2024

Author: Manoj Kumar Garg Bench: Manoj Kumar Garg [2024:RJ-JD:22038]
 HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE FOR RAJASTHAN AT  JODHPUR  S.B. Criminal Appeal (Sb) No. 2186/2023 Manisha W/o Vikas Kumar D/o Pradeep Kumar, Aged About 33 Years, R/o Sadpura, At Present Bairasar Chhota, P.s. Rajgarh,

----Respondents For Appellant(s) : Mr. Rakesh Matoria For Respondent(s) : Mr. Mukesh Trivedi, PP

HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE MANOJ KUMAR GARG Order 15/05/2024 Instant criminal appeal under Section 372 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the appellant/complainant against the judgment dated 31.03.2023, passed by learned Additional Sessions Judge No.1, Rajgarh, District Churu in Sessions Case No.80/2014 (20/2010) whereby the learned trial court acquitted the accused-respondent Nos.2 & 3 from the offences under Sections 498-A & 307/34 IPC.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge No.1, Rajgarh, District Churu
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Brief facts of the case are that on 01.05.2010, the appellant- complainant gave a parcha bayan to the Police to the effect that her marriage was solemnized with accused Vikas on 30.03.2010 and his parents gave sufficient dowry in her marriage in accordance with their capacity.
After few days of marriage, the in-laws of the appellant started harassing her mentally and physically for bringing [2024:RJ-JD:22038] (2 of 5) [CRLAS-2186/2023] less dowry.
On 30.04.2010, appellant's husband Vikas, her mother- in-law, father-in-law and sister-in-law gave brutal beatings to her and also tried to murder her by hanging.
Upon raising hue and cry, the neighbours came to her rescue.

On the basis of the said parcha bayan, Police registered the case against the accused persons and started Manisha vs State Of Rajasthan (2024:Rj-Jd:22038) on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9583685/
1 investigation.
On completion of investigation, the police filed challan only against accused Vikas and the trial court framed charges only against accused Vikas.
But subsequently on an application under Section 319 Cr.P.C. being allowed, the trial court took cognizance against other accused persons including respondent Nos.2 & 3.
Thereafter, the trial court also framed the charges against the accused-respondent Nos.2 & 3.
All the accused persons denied the charges and claimed trial.
During the course of trial, the prosecution examined 17 witnesses and got exhibited certain documents.
Thereafter, statements of the accused persons including respondent Nos.2 & 3 were recorded under section 313 Cr.P.C.
In defecne, five documents were exhibited.

Upon conclusion of the trial, the learned trial court vide impugned judgment dated 31.03.2023 while convicting and sentencing the accused Vikas for offence under Section 307 IPC, acquitted the accused-respondent Nos.2 & 3 from offences under Sections 498-A & 307/34 IPC.
Hence this criminal appeal against the acquittal of accused-respondent Nos.2 & 3.

Learned counsel for the appellant has submitted that there is ample evidence against the accused-respondent Nos.2 & 3 regarding commission of offence but the learned trial court has not considered the evidence and other aspects of the matter in its [2024:RJ-JD:22038] (3 of 5)
[CRLAS-2186/2023] right perspective and acquitted the accused-respondent Nos.2 & 3 from offence under Sections 498A & 307/34 IPC, whereas the learned trial court convicted the accused Vikas for offence under Section 307 IPC.
The learned trial court has committed grave error in acquitting the accused-respondent Nos.2 & 3.

Thus, the impugned judgment to the extent of acquitting the accused respondent No.2 & 3 deserves to be quashed and set aside and the accused-respondent Nos.2 & 3 ought to have been convicted and sentenced for offence under Sections 498-A & 307/34 IPC.
Heard learned counsel for the appellant and perused the impugned judgment as well as considered the material available on record.

On perusal of the impugned judgment, it appears that the learned trial court while passing the impugned judgment has considered each and every aspect of the matter and also considered the evidence produced before it in right perspective.
The learned trial court convicted the accused Vikas for offence under Section 307 IPC as there is ample evidence against him.
But in respect of the accused-respondent Nos.2 & 3, no specific averment has been made against them for commission of alleged offence.
There are major contradictions, omissions & improvements in the statements of the witnesses in respect to accused-respondent Nos.2 & 3.

The accused-respondent Nos.2 & 3 are ladies and the prosecution has completely failed to prove its case against the accused-respondent Nos.2 &
3 beyond all reasonable doubts and thus, the learned trial court has rightly acquitted the accused-respondent Nos.2 & 3 from offence under Sections 498A & 307/34 IPC.

[2024:RJ-JD:22038] (4 of 5) [CRLAS-2186/2023] In the light of aforesaid discussion, the appellant has failed to show any error of law or on facts on the basis of which interference can be made by this Manisha vs State Of Rajasthan (2024:Rj-Jd:22038) on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9583685/
2
Court in the judgment under challenge.
The learned trial court has rightly acquitted the accused-respondent Nos.2 & 3 from the offences.
The order passed by the learned trial court is detailed and reasoned order and the same does not warrant any interference from this Court.

In the case of 'Mrinal Das & others v. The State of Tripura, : reported in 2011(9) SCC 479,', the Hon'ble Supreme Court, after looking into many earlier judgments, has laid down parameters, in which interference can be made in a judgment of acquittal, by observing as under:
"An order of acquittal is to be interfered with only when there are "compelling and substantial reasons", for doing so.

entities.text: Mrinal Das & others v. The State of Tripura, : reported in 2011(9) SCC 479,
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If the order is "clearly unreasonable", it is a compelling reason for interference.

When the trial Court has ignored the evidence or misread the material evidence or has ignored material documents like dying declaration/report of ballistic experts etc.,the appellate court is competent to reverse the decision of the trial Court depending on the materials placed.

Similarly, in the case of State of Rajasthan v. Shera Ram alias Vishnu Dutta, reported (2012) 1 SCC 602,' the Hon'ble Supreme Court has observed as under:--
"A judgment of acquittal has the obvious consequence of granting freedom to the accused.

entities.text: State of Rajasthan v. Shera Ram alias Vishnu Dutta, reported (2012) 1 SCC 602
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This Court has taken a consistent view that unless the judgment in appeal is contrary to evidence, palpably erroneous or a view which could not have been taken by the court of [2024:RJ-JD:22038] (5 of 5) [CRLAS-2186/2023] competent jurisdiction keeping in view the settled canons of criminal jurisprudence, this Court shall be reluctant to interfere with such judgment of acquittal."
There is a very thin but a fine distinction between an appeal/revision against conviction on the one hand and acquittal on the other.

The preponderance of judicial opinion is that there is no substantial difference between an appeal/revision against acquittal except that while dealing with an appeal/revision against acquittal the Court keeps in view the position that the presumption of innocence in favour of the accused has been fortified by his acquittal and if the view adopted by the trial Court is a reasonable one and the conclusion reached by it had grounds well set out on the materials on record, the acquittal may not be interfered with.
Learned counsel for the appellant has failed to show any error of law or on facts on the basis of which interference can be made by this Court in the judgment under challenge.
In the facts and circumstances of the case, the present criminal appeal has no substance and the same is hereby dismissed.

The record of the court below be sent back forthwith.
(MANOJ KUMAR GARG),J 46-MS/-
